bib.title: BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure", Maarten Grootendorst, preprint (arXiv:2203.05794v1, 11 Mar 2022; no venue printed), 2022.

COVERAGE: 38,305 of 38,305 chars, all 10 pages. References (p8-10) were read for origins. Nothing skipped. Quotes join line breaks and repair end-of-line hyphens and ligatures. Page and section are given instead of offsets.

CLAIMS

1. BERTopic has the highest coherence on one of three datasets, the tweets. Top2Vec-Doc2Vec beats it on the other two (my reading of Table 1).
- number: TC .166 / .167 / .066, against T2V-Doc2Vec .192 / .171 / -.169
- setup: NPMI coherence, averaged over 10-50 topics in steps of 10, 3 runs per step, 15 runs per score. 20 NewsGroups (16,309 docs), BBC News (2,225), Trump tweets (44,253). OCTIS, all-mpnet-base-v2. LDA and NMF at default parameters. Means only, no variance or significance test.
- quote: "T2V-Doc2Vec .192 .823 .171 .792 -.169 .658" and "BERTopic-MPNET .166 .851 .167 .794 .066 .663"
- where: p5, Table 1

2. Author's reading of that table: best on the tweets, competitive elsewhere.
- number: none
- setup: as claim 1. The author ties this to light preprocessing, not to text length.
- quote: "It has the highest scores on the slightly preprocessed dataset, Trump's tweets, whilst remaining competitive on the thoroughly preprocessed datassets, 20 NewsGroups and BBC News."
- where: p6, §6.1

3. CTM beats BERTopic on topic diversity on all three datasets.
- number: CTM TD .886 / .819 / .855, against BERTopic .851 / .794 / .663
- setup: as claim 1. On Trump, T2V-MPNET's .698 also beats BERTopic.
- quote: "CTM .096 .886 .094 .819 .009 .855"; "it is consistently outperformed by CTM"
- where: p5 Table 1; p6 §6.1

4. Baselines on the only short-text dataset.
- number: LDA TC -.011, TD .502; NMF TC .009, TD .379
- setup: Trump tweets, as claim 1.
- quote: "LDA .058 .749 .014 .577 -.011 .502"; "NMF .089 .663 .012 .549 .009 .379"
- where: p5, Table 1

5. Results are stable across SBERT models, so the smaller MiniLM is preferable when GPU capacity is limited.
- number: MiniLM .159/.833, .170/.802, .060/.660; MPNET .166/.851, .167/.792, .066/.663
- setup: BERTopic with 4 encoders, 15 runs per score.
- quote: "BERTopic-MiniLM .159 .833 .170 .802 .060 .660"; "the smaller and faster model, "all-MiniLM-L6-v2", might be preferable when limited GPU capacity is available."
- where: p6, Table 2 and §6.2

6. Doc2Vec inside BERTopic fails on the tweets.
- number: TC -.088, TD .536
- setup: Table 2, Trump.
- quote: "BERTopic-Doc2Vec .173 .871 .168 .819 -.088 .536"; "Doc2Vec struggles with creating accurate representations of the Trump dataset."
- where: p6, §6.2

7. Top2Vec depends on Doc2Vec; swapping in MPNET drops both of its metrics on all datasets. BERTopic's separation of embedding from representation is offered as the reason it stays competitive.
- number: T2V-MPNET TC .068 / -.027 / -.213
- setup: Table 1, with HDBSCAN and UMAP parameters fixed between BERTopic and Top2Vec.
- quote: "T2V-MPNET .068 .718 -.027 .540 -.213 .698"
- where: p5 Table 1; p6 §6.2

8. Dynamic topics: BERTopic beats LDA Sequence on coherence on both datasets but loses on diversity on UN. The linear-evolution smoothing has no measurable effect.
- number: Trump TC .079 vs .009; UN TC .231 vs .173, TD .779 vs .820
- setup: 50 topics, per-timestep NPMI averaged, 3 runs. Trump tweets and UN general debates 2006-2015.
- quote: "LDA Sequence .009 .715 .173 .820"; "BERTopic .079 .862 .231 .779"; "BERTopic-Evolve .079 .863 .226 .769"
- where: p6, Table 3 and §6.3

9. Wall time: classical models are faster than neural ones, BERTopic and Top2Vec are similar given the same encoder, and CTM is much slower. The prose gives no seconds.
- number: 2 cores, 2.00GHz, 16GB GPU; 1000 to 43000 docs
- setup: Trump dataset, GPU available for embedding.
- quote: "All the models are run on a machine with 2 cores of Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU @ 2.00GHz and a Tesla P100-PCIE-16GB GPU."; "ranging from 1000 documents until 43000 documents with steps of 2000"; "the classical models, NMF and LDA, are faster than the neural network-based topic modeling techniques."
- where: p5 §5.3; p7 Fig 1 and §6.4

10. c-TF-IDF formula: concatenate each cluster into one document, then weight tf by log(1 + A / tf_t), where A is the average number of words per class.
- number: none
- setup: Eq. 2.
- quote: "we treat all documents in a cluster as a single document by simply concatenating the documents."; "taking the logarithm of the average number of words per class A divided by the frequency of term t across all classes. To output only positive values, we add one to the division within the logarithm."
- where: p3, §3.3

11. Why c-TF-IDF exists: centroid-based topic words assume spherical clusters.
- number: none
- setup: critique of Sia et al. and Top2Vec.
- quote: "a cluster will not always lie within a sphere around a cluster centroid."
- where: p1, §1

12. Why UMAP and HDBSCAN.
- number: none
- setup: design rationale, not tested in this paper. The noise benefit is only "expected".
- quote: "in high dimensional space, the concept of spatial locality becomes ill-defined"; "finds clusters of varying densities"; "allowing noise to be modeled as outliers. This prevents unrelated documents to be assigned to any cluster and is expected to improve topic representations."
- where: p2-3, §3.2

13. Topics can be reduced to a target count by merging.
- number: none
- setup: described, not evaluated.
- quote: "iteratively merging the c-TF-IDF representations of the least common topic with its most similar one, we can reduce the number of topics to a user-specified value."
- where: p3, §3.3

14. Representation can be tuned without re-clustering, and local (per-time or per-metadata) topics need no re-embedding.
- number: none
- setup: design property.
- quote: "increasing the n-gram of words in the topic representation, without the need to re-cluster the data."
- where: p7, §7.1

LIMITS

Conceded by the author:
- Single topic per document: "BERTopic assumes that each document only contains a single topic which does not reflect the reality that documents may contain multiple topics." HDBSCAN's probability matrix is only a partial proxy, and is not used in training (p8, §7.2).
- Topic words remain bag-of-words: "the topic representation itself does not directly account for that as they are generated from bags-of-words." Words can be redundant. MMR "was not explored in this study" (p8).
- Metrics are proxies: "they are just that, an indication." NPMI's link to human judgment "may only be the case for classical models and that this relationship might not exist with neural topic models (Hoyle et al., 2021)" (p5, §5.3).
- GPU: "the wall time is expected to increase significantly when embedding documents without a GPU." (p7).
- Many use cases "are not covered in this study" (p7).

Not shown (my reading):
- No noise or outlier share is reported on any dataset, and no test that removing noise improves topics.
- No clustering metric (NMI or similar), no human evaluation, no downstream task.
- No UMAP or HDBSCAN parameter values in the paper, only "fixed" (repository footnote, p4).
- No effect of document length is tested.
- Preprocessing and length are confounded: the one short-text dataset is also the one lightly preprocessed set.
- No variances. No tuning of LDA or NMF. The UN corpus size is not stated.

Internal inconsistencies:
- BERTopic-MPNET BBC TD is .794 in Table 1 and .792 in Table 2.
- §5.1 says Trump was "binned to 10 timesteps", while the Table 3 caption says "each of the 9 timesteps in each dataset" and "27 values".
- §6.4 questions Doc2Vec's stability, but §7.1 says "when a user does not have access to a GPU, Doc2Vec can be used to generate competitive results", despite TC -.088 on tweets.

Dated: 2022 v1 preprint with a P100 GPU. It predates any comparison with later encoders. "Competitive" is relative to five baselines only.

BUILDS ON (as printed):
- Clustering-embeddings approach: Sia et al. (2020); Angelov (2020), Top2Vec.
- Encoders: Reimers and Gurevych (2019), SBERT; Devlin et al. (2018); Song et al. (2020), MPNet; Cer et al. (2018); Le and Mikolov (2014).
- UMAP: McInnes et al. (2018).
- HDBSCAN: McInnes et al. (2017); McInnes and Healy (2017). Campello is not cited.
- TF-IDF: Joachims (1996).
- Curse of dimensionality: Aggarwal et al. (2001); Beyer et al. (1999).
- UMAP before clustering: Allaoui et al. (2020).
- Dynamic topics: Blei and Lafferty (2006).
- Baselines: Blei et al. (2003); Févotte and Idier (2011); Bianchi et al. (2020a), CTM.
- Metrics: Bouma (2009); Lau et al. (2014); Dieng et al. (2020) for diversity; Hoyle et al. (2021).
- Evaluation: Terragni et al. (2021), OCTIS.
- MMR: Carbonell and Goldstein (1998).

CODE: none in the paper. Equations as extracted, with fractions flattened:
- Eq. 2, p3: "Wt,c =tft,c · log(1 + Atft )"
- Eq. 3, p4: "Wt,c,i =tft,c,i · log(1 + Atft )"
Repositories (p4, footnotes): https://github.com/MaartenGr/BERTopic and https://github.com/MaartenGr/BERTopic_evaluation.

FIGURES:
- Figure 1, p7 (the only figure): "Computation time (wall time) in seconds of each topic model on the Trump dataset. Increasing sizes of vocabularies were regulated through selection of documents ranging from 1000 documents until 43000 documents with steps of 2000. Left: computational results with CTM. Right: computational results without CTM as it inflates the y-axis". It shows at a glance that CTM is the outlier and that encoder choice sets BERTopic's cost.
- Read off the rendered plot, approximate and not printed as numbers: CTM about 1,500 s, BERTopic-MPNET about 100 s, BERTopic-MiniLM about 60 s, classical models about 35-45 s, all at about 18,000 vocabulary. Do not cite these as paper-stated figures.
- The x-axis is vocabulary size, not documents. Legend colours for LDA differ between panels (brown left, purple right), so a caption must not rely on colour. A vector-style crop of the top of p7 is the likely route.
- No image of this paper exists in data-science/03-nlp/sources/images (grep empty).
- Table 1 and Table 2 (p5, p6) may teach better retyped than the figure, especially the Trump columns.

PROBLEMS: Equation fractions are flattened by extraction, but the §3.3 prose confirms the formula. Typos are the source's own ("clustering used", "preservers", a stray quotation mark in §3.2). Table values came from text extraction and were not checked against a page render; only p7 was viewed. No embedded instructions.

COMPARISON WITH THE NOTES

Files:
- /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/data-science/03-nlp/notes/03-topic-models-and-summarization.md
- /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/data-science/03-nlp/notes/07-llm-embeddings-as-features.md

MISMATCHES

A. 07:364, "assign those points to the nearest cluster, which BERTopic offers as an outlier-reduction step". NOT IN THE PAPER.
- "outlier" and "noise" appear once each, in the same sentence (§3.2), and it describes keeping noise out as a benefit.
- There is no reassignment step, and "reduce_outliers" and "outlier reduction" are absent.
- This may be a library feature, but I did not check the library. The sentence needs a separate read source (library docs) or rewording. It should not lean on the arXiv citation at 07:324.

B. 03:247 "For short texts..." and 03:480 "Short texts or where...". NO DIRECT EVIDENCE.
- The paper never claims a short-text advantage. "short-text" occurs once in its own text: "To represent more recent data in a short-text form" (§5.1).
- The support is one dataset: Trump TC .066 against LDA -.011 and NMF .009, with a coherence of low absolute size and TD behind CTM and T2V-MPNET.
- The author credits "slightly preprocessed", and length is not varied, so length and preprocessing are confounded.
- NPMI may not track human judgment for neural models (§5.3).
- Doc2Vec-based BERTopic scores TC -.088 on the same data, so any gain depends on the encoder.
- Defensible wording: BERTopic had the top coherence on the one tweet dataset in this paper, with coherence caveats. The note's bare recommendation is not sourced here.

C. 03:480 "where word order and meaning matter". OVERSTATED.
- "Word order" is not in the paper. It says bag-of-words ignores "the context of words in a sentence" (p1).
- §7.2 concedes the topic words themselves are still bags of words, so context only helps at the clustering stage.
- 03:247's "where LDA's bag of words hurts" has the same gap, though the paper's motivation does support it.

D. 07:324 "three steps". DIFFERENT SPLIT.
- The paper's steps are embed; reduce and cluster; c-TF-IDF (p2, §3).
- The note's are UMAP, HDBSCAN, c-TF-IDF, leaving embedding as already done. This is minor and harmless in context, but it is not the paper's count.

E. 07:324 "A cluster of vectors means nothing to a reader". DIFFERENT MOTIVE.
- The paper's stated reason for c-TF-IDF is to replace centroid-proximity word selection, since clusters are not always spherical (p1). Readers needing a name is not the argument it makes.
- "K-means forces every film into a cluster" is also the note's framing. The paper only says unrelated documents stay unassigned, and it mentions k-Means just via Allaoui et al. The substance is compatible.

F. 07:339-342 c_tf_idf code. SMALL DEVIATION FROM EQ. 2.
- The code divides tf by each cluster's total. Eq. 2 uses term frequency with no such normalisation; the paper's only L1 step is in §4.1 for smoothing.
- This does not change ranking within a cluster, so the printed top terms are unaffected. Weights differ across clusters.
- A, tf_t and log(1+...) all match. `stop_words` and `min_df=2` are the note's choices.

G. OMISSION in both notes. The single-topic-per-document assumption (§7.2) appears in neither. Note 03 defines a document as "a mixture of topics" (03:107) and then offers BERTopic as the modern route (03:247) without this trade-off, which is the author's first listed weakness. Also missing are the NPMI caveat and CTM's diversity lead.

H. 07:364 "The cost is the 54% of films labelled noise". The number is the note's own run and is correctly unattributed. The paper reports no noise share, so it neither confirms nor bounds this.

TENSION, not a citation error
- 03:196 says NMF is worth trying first on short text. On Trump, NMF beats LDA on TC (.009 vs -.011) but has the lowest TD of all models (.379 vs .502).
- 03:217 says `c_v` "Correlates best with human judgement". The paper uses NPMI and warns the link may fail for neural models. Comparing LDA with BERTopic by coherence therefore inherits that caveat.

MATCHES
- Preprint status and the arXiv ID (07:324).
- Distance contrast rationale for UMAP (§3.2).
- HDBSCAN "varying density" and noise (§3.2).
- Concatenating a cluster's text and finding what distinguishes clusters (§3.3).
- The references.md:37 row summary, and its PDF path, which exists.
- 03:247's pipeline order.

Unattributed, not from the paper: the note's UMAP and HDBSCAN parameter values (07:329-330). The paper prints none. Campello 2013 (07:324) is the note's own citation, not one the paper uses.

Possible sharpen: §6.2 and §6.4 directly support 07's use of MiniLM (Table 2 stability, "a good trade-off between speed and performance"). Note 07 does not currently draw on them.
